title: Call w/ Blacksburg landlord — lease + deposit
notes_markdown:
### Lease

- Old Blacksburg lease runs to May 31, 2027; subletter (a VT master's student) takes over Sep 1
- Landlord OK with a formal lease assignment instead of a sublet if the new tenant passes the application — $50 fee, paid by the tenant
- David stays on the hook until the assignment is signed

### Deposit

- Deposit to be returned to David once the assignment is signed, minus any damage from the walkthrough
- Walkthrough was done Aug 7: one stained carpet patch in the bedroom, nail holes from the bookshelf
- Gary estimates ~$120 for carpet cleaning; nail holes "normal wear"
- Refund by mailed check or Zelle — David asked for Zelle

### To do

- [ ] Send Gary the walkthrough photos from Aug 7
- [ ] Forward the new tenant's application link
- [ ] Update forwarding address with USPS (already done? check)
- [ ] Confirm deposit amount in writing

transcript.text: Hello?
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Hi, Gary? It's David Barron, from the, um, the unit on the second floor. I'm on speaker, sorry, I'm in California now.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: David, right, right. California. How's the weather?
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Cold, honestly. Nobody warned me about August here.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Ha! That's what they say. Okay, so you got my email about the lease?
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Yeah, that's why I'm calling. So the — the person taking over, she's a master's student, she's been there since the first basically.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: The young lady. Yes, she came by for the keys.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Right. So my question is, can we just make it official? Like instead of a sublet, put it in her name?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: We can do an assignment. She fills out the application, there's a fifty dollar fee, that's on her, and if it goes through she takes over the lease through end of May.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Okay great. And until then I'm still, um—
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Until it's signed you're still the one on the lease, yes. If she doesn't pay, I call you.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Sure. That's fair. She'll pay, she's very, uh, organized.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: They usually are, the grad students. Better than the undergrads, I'll tell you that.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Ha. Okay. And then the deposit. Does that come back to me once it's signed over?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Once the assignment's signed, yes, I return your deposit and she pays her own. Minus anything from the walkthrough.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Right, we did that the seventh. What did you, um, what did you end up seeing?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Let me find it. Okay. Carpet in the bedroom, there's that spot by the window.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Yeah, that was — that was there, I think, partially, but yeah.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I'll be fair, it'll need a cleaning, maybe a hundred twenty. And the holes from the shelf.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: The bookshelf, yeah. I anchored it to the wall because it was wobbly.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Holes are normal. I'm not charging for holes. Just the carpet.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Okay, that's fair. A hundred twenty is fine. Can you put that in an email, just so I have it?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I'll put it in writing. How do you want the money?
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Can you do Zelle?
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I can do Zelle. My daughter set it up. I'll need the email or phone for it.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: I'll send it in the email reply. And I'll send the photos from the walkthrough, I took a bunch.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Sure, send the photos. Is your mail getting forwarded? I've got one envelope here, looks like a bank.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Oh. Um. I thought I did the forwarding. I'll check. Can you just hand it to her, or — actually, can you mail it on? I'll send you where.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: I'll mail it. Send me the address.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Will do. Okay, so: she does the application, I send photos, you confirm the deposit in writing.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: That's it. Good luck out there. You doing the start-up thing?
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Yeah, trying to.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Well. Eat something besides avocado toast.
transcript.speaker: Gary

transcript.text: Ha, I'll try. Thanks Gary.
transcript.speaker: Me

transcript.text: Take care now.
transcript.speaker: Gary
